issues.failure_explanation: The displayed Gram-matrix decomposition first has lower-right entry \(\gamma^2\|x+y\|^2\), but the Weyl argument replaces the base block by one with lower-right entry 1 and also retains that term in the perturbation. Even for that displayed base block, its minimum eigenvalue is \(\min\{\sigma_{\min}^2(B),1\}\), not \(\sigma_{\min}^2(B)\). The claimed bound is false: with \(B=e_1\), \(x=e_2\), \(y=e_1\), and \(\gamma=1\), its right side is \(1+\sqrt2\), while \(\kappa([e_1,e_1+e_2])=(3+\sqrt5)/2>1+\sqrt2\).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, a repair must replace the invalid Weyl decomposition and prove a valid positive lower bound for the smallest singular value.
issues.overall_effect: The paper's general condition-number growth bound under no assumptions is not established and is false as stated.
issues.title: Invalid lower singular-value bound in the column-addition theorem
issues.why_classification: The principal bound of the section fails on a simple full-rank example, and the source supplies no alternative argument yielding a comparable bound.

issues.failure_explanation: Writing \(t=\|B^Ty\|/\|x+y\|\), the proof needs \(t\le \sqrt{\varepsilon^2-1}/2\), whereas the stated hypothesis is \(t\le(\varepsilon^2-1)/4\). The latter does not imply the former when \(\varepsilon^2-1>4\). The source also does not ensure that the resulting denominator \(2\sigma_{\min}^2(B)+1-\varepsilon\) is positive.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the hypothesis by the inequality actually needed and add conditions ensuring all denominators and square roots define a real finite bound.
issues.overall_effect: Item 2 is unsupported even independently of the defective bound in item 1.
issues.title: The hypothesis in item 2 does not imply the inequality used
issues.why_classification: A contained correction is possible, but it materially changes the allowed parameter regime and requires rechecking positivity of the final estimate.

issues.failure_explanation: For \(X=0\), the proof identifies \(\|Y\|^2/\sigma^2\) as central chi-square with \(m\) degrees of freedom. Its tail at \(\varepsilon^2/\sigma^2\) corresponds to \(\Gamma(m/2,\varepsilon^2/(2\sigma^2))/\Gamma(m/2)\), while the paper's definition gives the argument \(\varepsilon^2/\sigma^2\). Thus the theorem is incompatible with its own definition at zero noncentrality.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Change the zero-argument definition to use \(\Gamma(M,\beta^2/2)/\Gamma(M)\) and propagate that convention consistently.
issues.overall_effect: All central-noise specializations using the paper's Marcum-Q notation are wrong as written.
issues.title: The Marcum-Q definition at zero has the wrong gamma-function argument
issues.why_classification: A single local correction reconciles the definition with the distribution calculation and preserves the intended results.

issues.failure_explanation: The inner product with an \(m\)-dimensional column of \(Q^\perp\) must sum over all \(m\) coordinates, not only the first \(m-n\). The displayed covariance computation therefore does not prove the asserted covariance matrix or independence.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redo the covariance sums over indices 1 through \(m\), then invoke joint Gaussianity to infer independence from zero covariance.
issues.overall_effect: The stated proof that projected isotropic Gaussian coordinates remain independent is invalid, so subsequent projection and least-squares arguments lack this established input.
issues.title: The projected Gaussian covariance calculation omits coordinates
issues.why_classification: The claim is preserved by a short standard correction to the index ranges and independence argument.

issues.failure_explanation: When \(m=n\), the claimed Marcum-Q order is \(M=0\), although Definition def:marc-func requires \(M>0\). The orthogonal complement is then zero-dimensional and the stated formula is not defined.

failure_location.quote: Let \( Q \) be an orthonormal \( m \times n \) matrix with \( m \geq n \)

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Require \(m>n\), or state and prove a separate deterministic zero-dimensional case.
issues.overall_effect: The theorem does not cover the square case despite explicitly allowing it.
issues.title: Projection theorem includes a zero-dimensional complement outside its definitions
issues.why_classification: A standard boundary-case restriction or separate one-line case preserves the substantive positive-dimensional result.

issues.failure_explanation: No full-column-rank assumption is imposed. If \(\operatorname{rank}(B)<n\), the orthogonal complement of the column space has dimension \(m-\operatorname{rank}(B)\), not \(m-n\), so the asserted distribution has the wrong degrees of freedom.

failure_location.quote: Let \( B \) be an \( m \times n \) matrix with \( m \geq n \)

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Assume that \(B\) has full column rank, or replace \(m-n\) throughout by \(m-\operatorname{rank}(B)\).
issues.overall_effect: The probability formula is false for rank-deficient matrices covered by the statement.
issues.title: Projection corollary uses column count instead of rank
issues.why_classification: A local standard rank condition or rank-based parameter fixes the result without changing its method or rate.

issues.failure_explanation: The assumptions allow \(X=0\) and \(m-n=100\). Then \(\mathbb E\|P_Q^\perp Y\|^2=100\,2^{-16}\), so Markov's inequality gives \(\mathbb P(\|P_Q^\perp Y\|>0.1)\le 100/(65536\cdot0.01)\approx0.1526\), contradicting the claimed lower bound 0.9734.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Withdraw the uniform numerical lower bound or add a quantitatively sufficient lower bound on \(\|X\|\) and recompute the probability.
issues.overall_effect: The paper's concrete illustration that the probability is uniformly substantial for tall matrices is false.
issues.title: The claimed 0.9734 projection probability is false
issues.why_classification: The displayed numerical claim must be abandoned or materially restricted, though the general distribution formula can remain.

issues.failure_explanation: The squared, variance-normalized quantities \(Z_1^2/\sigma^2\) and \(Z_2^2/\sigma^2\), not the norms \(Z_1,Z_2\), have chi-square distributions. Consequently the noncentral-F threshold must involve \((\varepsilon_2/\varepsilon_1)^2\), and the event is an upper-tail event because the proof obtains \(Z_2/Z_1\ge\varepsilon_2/\varepsilon_1\). The formula is also undefined at the explicitly allowed value \(\varepsilon_1=0\).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reformulate the ratio using \(Z_1^2\) and \(Z_2^2\), use the squared threshold and the appropriate noncentral-F survival probability, and handle \(\varepsilon_1=0\) separately.
issues.overall_effect: The central exact probability formula for the normalized noisy residual is wrong, invalidating probability guarantees derived from it.
issues.title: Norms are mistaken for chi-square variables in the least-squares theorem
issues.why_classification: The distributional architecture can be retained, but the theorem's exact formula and tail orientation require a substantive contained recalculation.

issues.failure_explanation: Singular values of the diagonal block depend on \(|\gamma|\), not \(\gamma\). For negative \(\gamma\), the displayed maxima and minima are wrong; for \(\gamma=0\), item 3 divides by zero. No full-column-rank assumption is given even though finite \(\kappa(B)\), \(B^\dagger\) as its reciprocal singular-value factor, and the asserted minimum-singular-value manipulation require it.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use \(|\gamma|\), treat \(\gamma=0\) separately, and impose the rank assumptions needed for finite condition numbers.
issues.overall_effect: The theorem does not hold over its stated real-parameter and arbitrary-matrix scope.
issues.title: Singular-value bounds mishandle negative and zero gamma and rank deficiency
issues.why_classification: Standard local domain and absolute-value corrections preserve the substantive positive, full-rank case.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof derives the second expression by factoring \([B,c\gamma]=[Q,c]\operatorname{diag}(R,\gamma)\). The first expression comes from a different factorization using \([Q,c\gamma]\operatorname{diag}(R,1)\). There is no equality between the two resulting upper bounds in general.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: State the two expressions as separate upper bounds rather than equating them, and prove each from its corresponding factorization.
issues.overall_effect: Item 3 overstates two separately valid-style estimates as an identity.
issues.title: Two distinct condition-number bounds are asserted to be equal
issues.why_classification: A short local reformulation preserves both intended estimates without altering downstream arguments.

issues.failure_explanation: The cited formula uses the residual of \(c\) against \(B\), while the theorem defines \(r\) as the residual of \(c\gamma\). These residuals differ by \(|\gamma|\), so retaining the additional factors of \(\gamma\) in the formula double-counts the scaling. The displayed minimization also omits the norm around \(c\gamma-Bz\).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either redefine \(r\) as the residual of \(c\) or rescale every occurrence of \(r\) in the formula consistently, while adding the missing norm and admissible-parameter conditions.
issues.overall_effect: The condition-number estimate is not valid for general \(\gamma\), although its \(\gamma=1\) specialization can survive.
issues.title: Residual scaling is inconsistent in the final condition-number theorem
issues.why_classification: The theorem's residual meaning and quantitative formula must be changed for the advertised general scaling parameter, but the underlying factorization approach remains usable.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Assume \( B \) is an \( m \times n \) full rank matrix \( (m > n) \) and \( X\in \mathrm{span}(B^{\perp})
Assume \( B \in M_{m\times n}(\mathbb{R}) \) with columns of norm 1, \( q\in \mathbb{R}^{m} \), such that \( \|q\|_2=1 \).

issues.failure_explanation: The statement never defines \(q\) or relates it to \(X,Y\), yet its conclusion concerns \([B,q]\). It also omits the unit-column assumptions on \(B\) and the normalization \(\|q\|=1\) required by cor:cond-ls. Therefore neither cited result applies to the displayed matrix.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: No complete source-supported repair identified; at minimum, define \(q\) from \(X,Y\), specify the residual to which thm:noise-ls applies, and impose or replace the unit-column hypotheses needed by cor:cond-ls.
issues.overall_effect: The main bridge from the noise model to a condition-number probability guarantee is ill-defined.
issues.title: The probabilistic condition-number corollary uses an undefined q and missing hypotheses
issues.why_classification: The corollary's central random matrix is undefined and the required hypotheses are absent, so no stated guarantee survives without reconstructing the argument.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: The proof follows by recognizing that $\frac{1+\sqrt{1 -  \|r\|_2^2}}{ \|r\|_2}$ is a decreasing function of $\|r\|_2$

issues.failure_explanation: If \(a=\varepsilon_1/\varepsilon_2\) and \(\|r\|\ge1/\sqrt{1+a^2}\), monotonicity gives the multiplier \(\sqrt{1+a^2}+a\), not \(\varepsilon_1\sqrt{1+a^2}\). The displayed factor has a different dependence and can even tend to zero as \(\varepsilon_1\to0\), which cannot bound a condition number.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the multiplier by the value obtained by evaluating the decreasing function at the probability threshold and revise downstream products accordingly.
issues.overall_effect: Even after defining \(q\) and repairing the probability theorem, the stated condition-number magnitude is wrong.
issues.title: The deterministic multiplier in cor-main does not follow from the decreasing function
issues.why_classification: The correction is contained but materially changes the quantitative guarantee and all iterative growth factors.

issues.failure_explanation: Each \(E_i\) compares condition numbers of individual columns, which are normalized and have condition number 1; such events do not telescope to a bound for the growing prefixes or for \(\hat Q\). At iteration \(i\), the previous prefix has \(i-1\) columns, so the projection dimensions required by cor-main would be \(m-i+1\) and \(i-1\), not \(m-i\) and \(i\). In particular, the displayed formula divides by zero at \(i=n=m\), a case explicitly allowed.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redefine \(E_i\) using prefixes \(\hat Q[:,1:i]\), recompute the projection degrees of freedom and probability parameters at every iteration, and then redo the union-bound and telescoping argument.
issues.overall_effect: The final advertised probabilistic QR condition-number guarantee is not proved and is undefined in the square case.
issues.title: The QR iteration corollary uses single columns and wrong degrees of freedom
issues.why_classification: A systematic but contained reconstruction of the iteration indexing may yield a comparable product bound; the current argument itself cannot establish it.
